title: the first-run code in no journal or file others read; a PRODUCTION box rotates its exposed passphrase (D-1092); no passphrase from a caller's environment
note: basis 'shown' means shown by the card's local runs (no Docker, no systemd, no Windows, stand-ins); the container rehearsal was not run by the card.

findings.claim: the first-run wizard's one-time code went to stdout, which trialbox-firstrun.service sends to the system journal, and outside WSL2 to /etc/issue.d/trialbox-firstrun.issue, a file every local user reads (H96-09); fixed: box-install.sh show_code writes it to stdout only when stdout is a terminal, else to the controlling terminal, and with no terminal to the virtual console directly and a root-only 0600 file in the passwd home (made new, a link refused, removed when the answers are in); TB_ISSUE_DIR is gone

the box rehearsal (tools/rehearse_box/box.sh) runs install.sh and never box-install.sh --firstrun, so the rule has no real-path check there; the first-run step runs in the box-run rehearsal (tests/rehearsal/box-run, its getent shim now names the VM's root home) and the cloud box run (deploy/gcp/box-install-run.sh reads the root-only file), neither run in this session

on a box whose screen shows a graphical login (a desktop install) the code written to the virtual console is not seen; the root-only file is the way there (runbook 16 says so). On a VM the virtual console is its display, not a serial console a hypervisor logs; not shown on real hardware or a VM

the code shown on a terminal stays in that terminal's scrollback, and a site that turns on sudo's I/O logging (log_output) would record it with the session; the code is single use and voided after five wrong codes

a box installed before H-97 holds its first-run code in its journal and, outside WSL2, in /etc/issue.d until the next first run removes that file; a code already used opens nothing, and a box still waiting for its owner gets a new code at its next first run

rc1 refused tools.keys rotate-kek on a PRODUCTION box, so a box sealed under an exposed passphrase could not rotate it (H96-04); fixed by D-1092: a passphrase box rotates to a new passphrase from a root-only file or stdin, with no escrow set, as the audit event keys.rotate_kek (who, when, the box, the two KEK ids; never a value), refused without an audit folder; every other rotate-kek and key ceremony stays refused there

keys.rotate_kek is appended by the host into the audit folder (the audit volume's mount point on a box) beside the audit writer, as the escrow events are; that a concurrent append keeps the chain was not run on a box with the stack up
the Windows installer's window (wsl.exe owning the console) as the controlling terminal of box-install.sh under WSL2 is stood in for by a pty; not run on Windows

the KEK passphrase from a caller's environment was still honoured outside the installers (the review of H-96, L-2): tb_common.kek load_kek derived the KEK from TB_KEK_PASSPHRASE in the process environment, the nightly audit signer's container was given -e TB_KEK_PASSPHRASE (a caller's value in its configuration, docker inspect), and the restic key step forwarded it; fixed: load_kek refuses the process environment's value (the KEK file, read first, and tools.keys' own mapping unchanged), the signer is never given the name, the restic step forwards only TB_KEK_FILE

on a host with no TPM, site keys already sealed under the passphrase were a WARN on every box, PRODUCTION too (H-96's L-3); fixed by the integrator's ruling 7104745003: a WARN listed in deploy/site/poc-stops.jsonl on a PoC box (the box's recorded environment decides), else a FAIL; both name the action, reseal under a TPM
